news.title: Oliver Baumann says Julian Nagelsmann apologized after World Cup benching
news.lede: Germany goalkeeper Oliver Baumann has opened up about one of the toughest moments of his career after Julian Nagelsmann opted to restore Manuel Neuer as the starting goalkeeper for the World Cup. Baumann had established himself as Germany’s No. 1 leading up to the tournament, but Nagelsmann, leaning on input from some key players, ultimately turned back to Neuer for football’s biggest stage. While the decision was undoubtedly disappointing for Baumann, the goalkeeper sayid that the ex-Germany coach, who was recently replaced by Jürgen Klopp, reached out afterward to discuss everything openly. “He [Nagelsmann] was sorry about how everything turned out in the end.

news.title: Gianni Infantino promised Morocco 2030 World Cup final in exchange for support, says report
news.lede: Gianni Infantino's efforts to contain the growing crisis surrounding his FIFA presidency have reportedly taken another dramatic turn, with claims that he offered Morocco the right to host the 2030 FIFA World Cup final in exchange for political backing as pressure over his leadership continues to mount. Football News: Reports suggest Gianni Infantino offered Morocco the 2030 World Cup final in a bid for political support as he faces pressure over his FIFA leadership. FIFA denies the allegations.

In recent decades the city of Salé, just across the river from Rabat on Morocco’s Atlantic coast, has undergone a remarkable transformation. At the start of this century it was a gritty working-class area, whose old town was still weathered enough to serve as a body double for the Somali capital Mogadishu in the film Black Hawk Down. But in recent decades, under the country’s autocratic government, the area has been transformed beyond measure, and largely beyond control.

news.title: The Club World Cup deals the knockout blow to Infantino
news.lede: Aleksander Ceferin, president of European football's governing body (UEFA), and Nasser Al-Khelaifi, chairman of the European Club Association, are holding an anticipated meeting in the city of Salzburg. Tension is rising between their organisations and world football's governing body (FIFA), specifically against its president Gianni Infantino. According to the "talkSPORT" network, the root of that tension lies in the possibility of the European clubs withdrawing from the 2029 Club World Cup, following UEFA's decision regarding the national teams in relation to the World Cup. Spanish newspaper "AS" reported that there is as yet no agreement between the European Club Association and FIFA to stage the 2029 Club World Cup, which makes talk of boycotting the tournament inaccurate for now.

news.title: Neymar dismisses father's claim of 2030 World Cup return
news.lede: Brazil forward Neymar has brushed aside his father's suggestion that he could still return to the national team for the 2030 World Cup, insisting the decision rests with him alone. Neymar replied to his father's comments with a light-hearted quip: "It's not my dad playing!" Earlier, during the sixth Neymar Jr. Project Institute Auction, Neymar's father had expressed hope that his son's international career might not be over.

news.title: Manchester United consider World Cup star if £60m bid for Lewis Hall is rejected by Newcastle
news.lede: The Red Devils are keen to strengthen at left-back this summer, with Newcastle defender Hall their no.1 target. Michael Carrick is short of options on the left side of defence, with Luke Shaw their only senior player that is a specialist in the role. And with Champions League football returning to Old Trafford this season, United will need a bigger squad to rotate, making this position a priority area. Top of their wishlist has been Hall, who has earned a strong reputation at Newcastle since joining the club in 2024.

news.title: The Times: Infantino Offers Morocco 2030 World Cup Final in Return for Support
news.lede: Rabat - FIFA President Gianni Infantino has reportedly offered Morocco the right to host the 2030 FIFA World Cup final in exchange for continued political support as he faces growing pressure over his leadership, The Times reported today. The report claims Infantino promised Morocco the tournament's showpiece match at the under-construction Hassan II Stadium in Casablanca, which is expected to become the world's largest football stadium with a capacity of around 115,000 spectators. Morocco has remained one of Infantino's closest allies during his time as FIFA president, as the Swiss official is relying on Rabat’s backing as opposition to his leadership grows following a series of controversial decisions. The newspaper added that Infantino has been holding meetings in Rabat in an effort to secure support from football associations ahead of the 2027 FIFA presidential election.

news.title: He has no intention of giving up - Infantino gives the World Cup final to Morocco in exchange for support
news.lede: Almost everyone has turned against him, but Gianni Infantino has no intention of giving up. He wants to run for a new term as FIFA president, but this time it will be challenging given that his support is very thin. There are few who have not turned their backs on him, including representatives of the Moroccan Football Federation. As the British "Times" has learned, Infantino has offered the Moroccan federation to host the 2030 World Cup finals in exchange for his support at the FIFA congress that will decide on his new term.
